content: If someone is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call emergency services (911). For other cases, contact a poison control center without delay. In the United States, you can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. While taking this medication, your doctor may recommend laboratory or medical tests, such as hearing evaluations or kidney function assessments, to monitor your condition and the medication's effects. It is essential to attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose of this medication and are taking it to prevent infection before a scheduled surgery, take the missed dose as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next dose, continue with your regular dosing schedule as directed and consult your doctor or pharmacist promptly for a revised dosing plan. If you are using this medication to treat hepatic encephalopathy and miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or suitable for you. It is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs. To reduce the risk of infection after intestinal surgery, take this medication as prescribed by your doctor, typically for three or four doses the day before surgery. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. To minimize the risk of hearing loss and other side effects, use the lowest effective dose for the shortest possible duration. Do not increase your dose, take it more frequently, or use it for a longer period than prescribed. If you are taking this medication for hepatic encephalopathy, ensure you take it at evenly spaced intervals for optimal effectiveness. To help you remember, take it at the same times each day. Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. Before taking neomycin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other aminoglycoside antibiotics (e.g., tobramycin), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. High doses or prolonged use of neomycin may impair your body's ability to absorb certain foods, nutrients (e.g., iron, vitamins A and B-12), and drugs (e.g., digoxin, warfarin). Neomycin may also reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine). This medication is not recommended for use during pregnancy. Although there have been reports of harm to babies born to women using similar drugs, the risk may not be the same with this medication. It is unknown if this drug passes into breast milk. However, many doctors consider breastfeeding safe while using this medication. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your healthcare professional. Other medications that affect the kidneys or hearing may increase the risk of kidney damage or hearing loss if taken with neomycin. In the event of an overdose with severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. In the United States, you can call 1-800-222-1222.
